researcher_notes:
RESULT: NO CONFIRMED CURRENTLY-SOLD PRODUCTS. Recommendation: do NOT create a company or product records for AutoGuide Mobile Robots. The company no longer exists as an independent supplier; it was absorbed into Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR), which is already in the database.

=== COMPANY IDENTITY (historically confirmed) ===
AutoGuide Mobile Robots LLC was real. HQ: 2 Omni Way, Chelmsford, MA 01824, USA (R&D/HQ), with a manufacturing/assembly plant in Georgetown, Kentucky. Country: USA. History: spun out of Heartland Automation (Georgetown, KY systems integrator) in 2017 under CEO Rob Sullivan; Heartland was NOT part of the later sale but continued to manufacture AutoGuide robots. Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER) announced the acquisition 2019-10-21 and completed it 2019-11-14. Purchase price is reported inconsistently across trade press (The Robot Report: '$58M net of cash acquired'; other outlets cite $165M including earn-outs) - not material for this database, but noted as a source discrepancy. AutoGuide opened a German office in 2022. So: Teradyne Robotics group ownership is CONFIRMED, alongside sister company MiR (acquired by Teradyne 2018) and Universal Robots.

=== WHY NO PRODUCTS ARE ENTERED (the decisive finding) ===
AutoGuide ceased to exist as a distinct supplier/brand. Evidence, in order of weight:

1. MERGER INTO MiR. AutoGuide Mobile Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots merged into a single Teradyne AMR unit; the integrated company officially became known as Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR) at the end of September 2022 (publicly reported March 2023). Source: https://www.therobotreport.com/teradyne-merges-amr-companies-autoguide-mir/ - 'By combining with AutoGuide, the portfolio will expand to include high payload AMR tuggers and forklifts that will operate on the MiRFleet software.' Teradyne's stated intent was one AMR supplier, not two.

2. NO ACTIVE WEB PRESENCE. The former company domain agmobilerobots.com has NO A record (DNS resolves MX/mail records only, via Proofpoint - i.e. mail routing retained, website gone); curl fails with 'Could not resolve host'. The alternate domain autoguidemobilerobots.com resolves but serves only a parked-domain lander stub (114-byte HTML redirecting to /lander), not a company site. No official manufacturer source for specs exists anymore.

3. NOT IN THE CURRENT MiR CATALOG. MiR's live product page (https://www.mobile-industrial-robots.com/products/robots, fetched 2026-08-01) lists exactly: MiR250, MiR600, MiR1350, MC250, MC600, MiR1200 Pallet Jack. No MAX N10, no MAX N15, no MAX-N pallet stacker, no high-bay counterbalanced forklift, no heavy tugger. MiR's tugger offering today is the MiR Hook top module on MiR250 - a native MiR product, not AutoGuide-derived. The AutoGuide inheritance shows up as absorbed engineering know-how in the MiR1200 Pallet Jack (launched 2024-03), which MiR itself describes as leveraging 'high-payload AMRs that resulted from MiR's 2022 merger with AutoGuide' - technology transfer, not a surviving SKU.

4. CHANNEL CONFIRMATION. Former AutoGuide reseller RG Group now lists only 'MIR Mobile Industrial Robots' under Robotic Systems; its AutoGuide MAX N10 product URLs return 'Page Not Found'.

=== TRAP: STALE DIRECTORY LISTINGS (do not trust) ===
WebSearch surfaces many pages that still present the MAX N10 / MAX N15 / MAX-N Pallet Stacker / MAX-N High Bay Counterbalanced Forklift as 'available now', and one search-engine summary even asserted the product 'appears to be an actively marketed current offering as of 2026'. That is false. All such pages are unpruned trade-directory and reseller listings frozen around 2019-2021: materialhandling247.com/product/max_n10, automate.org/products/autoguide-mobile-robots/..., mmh.com/company/autoguide, industrialcontrol.com, rg-group.com (404), and search.therobotreport.com/listings/... (which still describes the company as active and even carries a misleading 'acq by Heartland Automation' slug - the Heartland relationship was the 2017 spin-OUT, i.e. the reverse direction). Anyone re-researching this company will hit these first; they are not evidence of current availability.

=== HISTORICAL SPEC FRAGMENTS (recorded for traceability only - NOT to be imported) ===
From the archived trade-press descriptions, the AutoGuide line was: MAX N10 modular AMR base, ~10,000 lb (~4,536 kg) tow capacity; MAX N15, ~15,000 lb (~6,804 kg); modular attachments for tugger / conveyor deck / pallet stacker / car mover / high-bay forklift; MAX-N Pallet Stacker described as a counterbalanced forklift picking from floor, conveyor or rack up to ~5 ft (~1,524 mm); 'SurePath' natural-feature LiDAR navigation, infrastructure-free (no tape/RFID/reflectors); up to 4 mph (~1.79 m/s); stopping accuracy 0.2 in (~5 mm); 1 degree heading control. These figures come from marketing copy on stale third-party directories, NOT from a manufacturer datasheet, and could not be cross-verified against any live official source. They must not be loaded into the matching database: the vendor cannot bid, and unverified KO values (max_payload, towing_capacity, lifting_height, max_speed) would corrupt matching either by wrongly qualifying or wrongly disqualifying.

=== ACTION FOR THE DATABASE ===
Skip this company entirely (consistent with the project rule: never create a supplier record without confirmed current products). The relevant live successor - MiR, incl. MiR1200 Pallet Jack - is already covered by the existing MiR supplier record; if MiR1200 Pallet Jack is not yet among MiR's products in the DB, that is the useful follow-up, not AutoGuide.
